summary:
The galaxy's space battles run in universe/battle.js (1018 lines), a pure sim with a variable timestep. It is laid out by galaxy/battles.js layBattle and run per pilot by galaxy/warfront.js on gcw.js's shared clock: a 12-minute step, 10 minutes of fighting (GCW.fight) and 2 of lull. Every battle kind uses the same objective chain on one ship: two shield generators at 120 hp each, then the bridge at 200, then the reactor at 260 (wars.js:305-310). The ship is the defender's flagship, or the Interdictor in an interdiction. Evacuations and blockades add runners on top of that chain. The 16 war systems fight only 5 kinds: 3 evacuation, 3 siege, 5 blockade, 3 interdiction and 2 ambush. None of them is 'assault' (systems.js). Siege is the same data as assault (battles.js:58,68). Ambush is a flagship plus one escort a side with 1.5x the fighters, its rocks are never read (battles.js:79,268,355), and its objective is still the full 3-phase chain.

The player sees objective markers ('Destroy/Defend: Shield generator' and, for a defender, 'Destroy: their flagship'; battleScene.js:272-287), lockable phase subsystems (attacker only; battle.js:985-993) and crew lines on events. The HUD is one line, the kind's text and a clock (WarHud.jsx; warText.js:64-71). There are no objective bars, no stage list and no end card. WarHud renders nothing during the lull (WarHud.jsx:12).

I ran the pure sim headless in Node, with nobody flying, for every kind, in both directions, over 3 seeds and at 20 Hz and 60 Hz (scripts in my scratchpad). No objective-driven attacker win came from the AI in GCW or the Clone or Remnant wars. The only AI attacker wins by objectives were the Empire against the Hutts. Blockades always go to the attacker on runners at 108-110 s. Evacuations always go to the defender on runners at 224-229 s at 20 Hz, and at 60 Hz Hoth splits (Empire wins at 274-275 s in 2 of 3 seeds). Liberator attacks lose on attacker tickets after 118-211 s at 60 Hz, with almost no objective damage. Raider attacks take the generators and bridge but never the MC80's reactor, and run out the 600 s clock.

The outcome also depends on the frame rate. With the same seed, Rebel losses in the first minute were 107, 88, 66 and 34 at 120, 60, 30 and 10 Hz, and the battle's result changed from a ticket loss at 161 s to a flagship kill at 451 s. It depends on the device tier (perSide 10/20/32) and on the arrival time too. A pilot arriving late gets a fresh fight whose clock starts at the elapsed time (battle.js:170), and the runners restart from their arrival.

The AI's damage to objectives is never shared; only pilots' damage is, through the fight tally, and only an attacker's (warfront.js:132-136, 211-215). Ticket, hull and runner endings are local, and addWin is keyed per side. So the two sides can both win the same step.

A single player decides everything: youShare is 4 on a 700 hp chain. A scripted pilot landing 1, 2.5 or 5 hits a second wins in 181, 76 or 41 s.

The AI's weaknesses:
- It re-targets every 0.35-0.6 s.
- Bombers re-roll their target each time (the defender's switch about 31 times a life).
- Interceptors weight bombers 0.12x and mob them. Imperial TIE bombers live a median 5.5 s and fire 0-1 torpedoes a battle.
- Once the enemy fighters are gone, dogfighters circle the battle's centre and attack nothing.
- There are no squads, wingmen, escorts, retreat, waves or difficulty scaling.
- Capitals never move. Their batteries pick a random enemy capital and a random point on it.

My recommendation has four parts:
- A fixed-step sim.
- A pure shared 'director' that computes objective HP, runner fates and the winner from seed + wall-clock t + tally totals. It uses a seeded AI pressure curve, pilot damage gated by stage open times, a defender intercept lever and pilot-count scaling, so every pilot sees the same battle, late joiners included.
- A seeded per-battle objective plan drawn from a registry of objective types.
- AI and capital upgrades, plus an escalation schedule and a real end and lull UX.

battle.js should be split into modules, each under the 800-line warning line and well under the 1500 ceiling.

rootCauses.title: A battle's outcome is per pilot, not shared: AI progress, tickets, hulls and runners are local, and both sides can win the same step
rootCauses.mechanism: Only pilots' objective damage goes into the fight tally, and only an attacker's (onMine and ctx.mine are gated by attacking()). The AI's torpedo damage (subHit with mine=false), attacker-ticket exhaustion, the attacker flagship's hull, runner escapes and the clock are all decided in each pilot's own sim. That sim differs by arrival time, frame rate, device tier and the pilot's own flying. Each pilot's 'over' event calls addWin(side()), keyed per side (winKey), so a defender whose sim ended on tickets and an attacker whose sim ended on the reactor both score a win. A late joiner gets a fresh fight: full capitals, objectives at full HP less pilots' shared damage, runners launching from their arrival. The fleet-war spec said the AI's progress would be 'a scripted curve, seeded by the battle's number. Every pilot's battle advances alike'; that was never built.
rootCauses.evidence: warfront.js:132-136, 210-215 (shared = tally - mine; onMine only if attacking); battle.js:369-388 (shared only adds pilots' damage), 694 (AI subHit mine=false), 868-872 (local ticket and clock end), 170 (clock = elapsed), 747-757 (runner wait starts at 0); warfront.js:327-336 (addWin(side()) on local over); gcw.js:135 winKey per side. Sims: elapsed=540 gives a fresh fight and a clock end at 600 with gens 84/80%; Hoth with elapsed=300 restarts runner 1 at arrival; tier low vs high changes Yavin from 'tickets at 260 s' to 'clock at 600 s'. fleet-war spec lines 221-236.

rootCauses.title: The sim is frame-rate dependent (variable dt, clamped to 0.1), and the outcome changes with the display rate
rootCauses.mechanism: update(dt) steps everything once per frame with the frame's dt. Turn caps (turnToward max = turn*dt), the head-on break window (dist<3), single shots per frame and the bomber firing cone all behave differently per step size. At low rates the nose snaps to its aim, so the agility gap (TIE turn 2.6 and interceptor 3.0 against X-wing 2.3 and Y-wing 1.7) disappears; at 60-120 Hz the Imperial dogfighters dominate mid-field. warfront.skip runs at dt 0.1 and the Vitest 'left to itself' test at 1/20, so neither matches a real 60 Hz frame.
rootCauses.evidence: dtprobe.mjs, same seed (yavin assault, Rebels attack), first 60 s: Rebel losses 107/88/66/34 and Imperial 54/53/59/55 at 120/60/30/10 Hz; Rebel torpedoes 3/0/10/49; gens dealt 0/1.3/17.9/87. The same with BATTLE.flak=0 (dtprobe2.mjs: 102/84/68/21), so it isn't point defence. dtrole.mjs: Rebel deaths mid-field 57 at 60 Hz against 8 at 10 Hz. Full battle: dt 1/60 'defender by tickets 161 s, dealt 1/4/0/0'; dt 1/30 'tickets 240 s'; dt 0.1 'flagship 451 s, dealt 120/121/201/156'. battle.js:835, 539, 484, 552-573; warfront.js:415-417; battle.test.js 'a battle left to itself' uses dt 1/20.

rootCauses.title: Battles end far too early or are pre-decided: blockades about 108 s, evacuations about 224-275 s, liberator attacks about 2-3.5 min on tickets
rootCauses.mechanism: (a) layBattle never passes tickets:false, so 220 attacker tickets drain in about 4 minutes of symmetric attrition (about 50 fighters a minute a side at 32 a side), and only the attacker's count ends the battle. (b) Runner routes run beside the fight. Blockade runners launch from the attacker's flagship position and fly 133 units to the planet without crossing the defender's line. Evacuation transports fly from the planet to 160 units beyond their own line, mostly outside the radius the attacker's fighters are pulled back into. They launch every 45 or 38 s, so the battle is decided as soon as the 3rd or 6th runner gets out. (c) The 10-minute clock only matters when nothing else ends it.
rootCauses.evidence: battles.js:344-360 (no tickets), 320-343 (routes); battle.js:870, 758-763. runners.mjs: Bespin, Naboo and Kashyyyk routes are 133 long with 'from→attacker flag 0'; Hoth and Yavin routes are 53-56% inside the radius; most runners escape with full HP ('hit 0 times'), and none were shot down at 20 Hz. 20 Hz matrix: blockade attacker wins at 108.2-109.5 s in all 6 runs; evacuation defender wins at 223.1-229 s in all 7. 60 Hz matrix: liberator and Separatist/New Republic/Hutt attacks lose on tickets at 118-211 s with gens damage of 0-21/120. Kamino blockade 108-110 s in every war.

rootCauses.title: The AI alone essentially never takes an objective chain
rootCauses.mechanism: Bombers are the only AI that hurts objectives (at aiShare 0.22). Their targets are re-rolled every retarget (0.35-0.6 s): attacker bombers flip 50/50 between a runner and a random phase subsystem, defender bombers pick a new random hull point on a random capital each time. Interceptors weight bombers 0.12x, so the side with fewer bombers (the Empire: 1.5 of 7.5 weight) gets mobbed before it crosses the 140-unit gap. The MC80's reactor sits inside its stern hull sphere: sweptHit returns the closest-approach k, so from the bow the hull sphere wins and only shots from astern reach it, while bombers come at the bow.
rootCauses.evidence: battle.js:399-415, 454-461, 422; wars.js:324-331 vs 482. bombers.mjs (Yavin): Imperial TIE bombers median life 5.5-5.7 s, closest approach 49-67 units, 0 torpedoes as attacker and 1 as defender over 112/108 deaths; Rebel bombers live 13-15 s and fire 268 torpedoes; defender bombers switch target 31 times a life. Every Empire-attacks-MC80 run shows reactor dealt 0/260 (e.g. Endor 121/121/201/0). Only AI attacker wins: Empire vs Hutts (Yavin 551 s, Mustafar 483 s).

rootCauses.title: Idle fighters orbit the centre: no strafing, no objective or turret attacks
rootCauses.mechanism: fighterTarget only returns enemy fighters, runners or you. With none, `want` points at the battle centre C and the fire gate (`if (!tp …) return`) stops all shooting. Once the defender's tickets and fighters are gone, the attacker's dogfighters circle forever while the reactor stalls.
rootCauses.evidence: battle.js:416-445, 476-478, 552. Yavin rebel attack timeline (dt 0.05): from 240 s the Imperials have 0 tickets and 0 fighters up, the Rebels 23-32 fighters up, and the reactor goes 96%→88% between 360 and 420 s, then the Rebel flagship dies to turbolasers at 444.4 s.

rootCauses.title: The player's damage dwarfs the AI's: a solo pilot finishes in about 40-180 s, while a defender has no shared lever
rootCauses.mechanism: A hit on an objective counts youShare 4 against a 700 HP chain, at the ship's cadence (about 5.5 shots a second). Nothing gates the stages in time or scales with the number of pilots. A defender's kills only change their own local sim; nothing a defender does reaches the shared tally.
rootCauses.evidence: battle.js:83-84, 943; scene.js:822 (cadence about 0.18 s), outfit.js punch. sim.mjs player=gunner on Yavin (Empire attacks MC80): pdps 1, 2.5 and 5 win at 181.0, 76.0 and 40.8 s. warfront.js:132-136 (defenders never add to the tally).

rootCauses.title: No end screen or lull UX, and a dead battle lingers
rootCauses.mechanism: After over, fighters keep flying without firing, batteries stop and nothing respawns, until the step's id changes at 12 minutes. WarHud reads the shared table only. It keeps showing '<objective> · m:ss left' after the local battle ended, and returns null in the lull, so the 'regrouping, the next in…' line is unreachable. The only feedback is the crew's won/lost lines when tookPart. universe/front.js emits an end card event that nothing renders.
rootCauses.evidence: battle.js:552, 850, 863; warfront.js:279-284; WarHud.jsx:12; warText.js:64-71; front.js:143-157 (event emitted, no consumer found).

rootCauses.title: Interdiction objectives are invisible: markers and shield are hard-wired to the defender's flagship
rootCauses.mechanism: With objectivesOn 'interdictor' the subsystems are on the Interdictor (objective: true, role 'escort'). battleScene still looks up the role==='flagship' cap for markers (its subs are []) and shows the shield bubble round the flagship. Locks work (b.targets uses objOf), but nothing is marked.
rootCauses.evidence: battle.js:188-189, 230-231, 236; battleScene.js:185-186, 274-283. Applies to Mustafar, Nevarro and Mandalore whenever the dark side defends (battles.js:271).

rootCauses.title: Set pieces ignore which side the player is on
rootCauses.mechanism: Hangar runs are laid in every team-1 Star Destroyer whatever the player's side. Their reactor only takes ctx.mine damage, which counts attackers' shots only. A Rebel defender can fly in but never blow it (dead end). An Imperial attacker can blow up their own ISD and score objective x2 for the Empire. Endor's moon generator and DS2 run count an Imperial attacker's shots too, and the run ends the battle with battle.end(REBELS). Hoth's ion cannon fires on team 1 whoever holds Hoth.

rootCauses.title: Static, unscripted AI structure: no squads, waves, retreat, capital manoeuvre or difficulty, and constant pressure on the player
rootCauses.mechanism: Every fighter decides alone, retargeting about 0.6 times a second (in sights 18% of the time). A pilot within 70 units of a fight always has 2 enemies on them (up to onYou 4). Respawns trickle individually 3-6 s after a death, in front of the line. Capitals never move: batteries fire at a random enemy capital and sphere, 40% of shots deliberately near misses, and point defence hits the nearest fighter. There are no escalation events, no dynamic difficulty and no ace behaviour beyond extra HP.
rootCauses.evidence: battle.js:438-443, 92, 320-327, 240-268, 578-621. ai.mjs: switch rate 0.61-0.69/s; modes engage 70%, extend 13-15%, break 9-11%, jink 5.5%. A player circling the attacked objective has 3.1 fighters on them on average and takes 5.0 shield/s at r=14 (13.7/s at r=30), against regen of 12/s that only starts after 5 s unhit. As a defender near their own flagship: 1.65 on them, 0.4/s. Hull penetration 0.0-0.3% of samples, outside the radius 0-3.7%, nearest teammate 7-13 units, so no clumping or suicides.

rootCauses.title: The specs' battle kinds are only partly built, and the dormant crew lines show it
rootCauses.mechanism: Siege has no gate phase except Scarif's set piece, and Coruscant gets no planetary shield. Ambush has no rocks and no single-bridge objective. 'runners', 'interdictor', 'blockade', 'escort' and 'gate' crew lines exist but warfront only ever says front/ask/join/gens/bridge/reactor/ace/intercept/won/lost. Runners have markers only at Hoth.
rootCauses.evidence: battles.js:58-80; allegiance spec :231-256; battleLines.js:26; warfront.js:226-335; hoth.js markers; HANDOFF-fleet-war.md 'Revision 3: left'.

proposals.title: Fixed-step sim and split battle.js into modules
proposals.description:
In battle.js update(dt): add an accumulator and step the sim at STEP = 1/30 s (at most 8 sub-steps a frame, drop the rest), concatenating each sub-step's events into the returned list. Then move code out:
- universe/battleAi.js: spawn, makeFighter, fighterTarget, bomberTarget and flyFighter as functions taking (b, ctx).
- universe/battleCapitals.js: fireBatteries, moveCapital, turnCapital and disable/wreck.
- universe/battleRunners.js: launchRunners, judgeRunners, flyRunners and addRunner.
battle.js keeps createBattle's wiring, bolts, hit, targets, info and end, about 450-550 lines. Each module stays under 800 lines (scripts/health/big-files.mjs WARN) and battle.js well under CEILING 1500. Keep the public interface front.js, warfront.js, battleScene.js and the set pieces use: teams, capitals, fighters, runners, bolts, phase, clock, over, you, attacker, defender, setYou, update, hit, fire, targets, info, end, disable, wreck, moveCapital, turnCapital, addRunner. warfront.skip(seconds) keeps working because frames of 0.1 become 3 sub-steps.
proposals.tests: For the same seed and inputs, the event log and a state hash (fighter positions to 1e-6, tickets, sub HP) are identical after 120 s whether update is called with dt 1/144, 1/60, 1/30 or 0.1. The existing battle.test.js, battles.test.js, warpieces.test.js and warfront.test.js pass unchanged. The 64-fighter performance test still passes. A line-count test asserts battle.js < 1500 and each new module < 800.

proposals.title: Shared battle director: one deterministic battle state for every pilot
proposals.description:
New pure module universe/battleDirector.js: createDirector({ plan, seed, length: 600 }) with state(t, value) → { stage, objectives: [{ id, hp, hpMax, down, opensAt }], runners: [{ i, launchedAt, k, hp, out, down }], winner, why, endsAt }. It depends only on the battle seed, the shared wall-clock seconds t = (now - battle.start)/1000 and tally totals.

AI pressure is P(t) = H·g(t)/T_ai:
- H is the chain's total HP.
- T_ai is seeded U[500, 760] s, so the AI alone finishes in 38-45% of battles.
- g has slope 1, rising to 1.5 after the final push at 480 s.
- P is reduced by defender intercept credits: P' = max(0, P - 8·value('int')).

The chain is consumed in plan order. Each objective's remaining HP is hpMax·scale - pilots' damage, read from key o:<id>. Parallel objectives in a stage share pressure equally, and overflow flows on.
- Pilot damage counts only from the stage's opensAt, a plan gate (assault [0, 150, 300] s), which bounds the shortest battle at about 5 minutes.
- Pilot scaling: scale = 1 + 0.5·min(5, n-1), where n = value('here:a') (each attacker pilot adds 1 once on joining).
- A hit counts 1·punch chain HP in place of youShare 4. Suggested chain: gens 2×140, bridge 300, reactor 420 = 1000.

warfront.js uses it:
- Sub HP and phase come from director.state (replacing battle.js's sharedSubs and subHp in the galaxy, via a new createBattle option director).
- b.end(winner, why) is called when the director says so; a local 'over' with no director winner is ignored.
- layBattle passes tickets:false (the battle.js:36 header's intent).
- AI torpedo hits on objectives become impacts only.
- Capitals die to AI fire only at director-scheduled times.
- addWin goes only to the director's winner.
- Defender pilots' bomber or runner-hunter kills add 1 to 'int' (a new ctx.mineAs(team, key) beside ctx.mine).

The universe map's front.js keeps the current local rules (no director passed). Keys use under 40 of the tally's 96, each matching the key regex.
proposals.tests: The battle state is path independent: state(t) computed cold equals the state stepped from 0 in 1 s steps (late joiners agree). It is monotone in t and in each tally value. Over 300 seeds with no pilots: attacker win rate per kind in [0.3, 0.6], median resolution 450-600 s. With one simulated solo attacker at 1.25 chain HP/s: median win between 270 and 450 s; with 4 pilots, never before the last gate plus 30 s. Each defender intercept lowers the attacker's win probability. warfront: two fronts (one per side) fed the same tally produce the same winner, and only that side gets addWin. A pilot joining at 540 s sees the same objective HP as one there from 0.

proposals.title: Runners that fly through the fight, and fates every pilot shares
proposals.description:
In battles.js layBattle:
- Evacuation: the route runs from the planet, through the battle's centre band (within lines·0.3 of C), past the attacker line's flank to a jump point radius·1.2 beyond it.
- Blockade: the route runs from 30 units behind the attacker's line, through the gap between the defender's flagship and its first escort, to the planet.
Runner i launches at absolute battle second i·every (not at arrival), its position is route(t - launchedAt), and it gets a seeded AI fate. The director (proposal 2) computes hp_i = hp - aiHit_i(t) - value('r:<i>') + 0.5·value('cover:<i>'), where aiHit_i is seeded with total in U[0.4, 1.4]·hp spread along the route, r:<i> is damage by the runner's enemies among the pilots, and cover:<i> counts kills by its friends within 25 of it. The runner escapes at route end with hp > 0. Generalise Hoth's 'Protect/Stop: transport n' markers into battleScene for every battle's runners, and say the dormant 'runners' and 'blockade' crew lines on launch.
proposals.tests: Every evacuation and blockade route is ≥60% inside the radius and passes within 25 units of the enemy line's axis segment. With no pilots, over 200 seeds the evacuation and blockade attacker win rate is in [0.3, 0.6] and no battle is decided before 300 s. A pilot joining at 300 s sees launched = floor(300/every)+1 with the same escaped and down set as one present from 0. Markers exist for runners in a Bespin and a Lothal battle.

proposals.title: Correctness fixes for objectives and set pieces
proposals.description: (a) battleScene.js:185-186, 274-283: find the objective ship with capitals.find(c => c.objective) instead of the defender's role==='flagship', for the shield bubble and the markers (interdiction). (b) hangar.js:28: lay runs only in the player's enemy's destroyers (team !== battle.you.team), and only count shots on a ship of the side being attacked by the shooter. Replace ctx.mine with a team-aware ctx.mineAs(team, key) so a Rebel defender's run can blow an Imperial ISD (key core-i) and an Imperial attacker can't wreck their own. (c) endor.js: the generator and the DS2 run count only the Rebel team's shots (team 0), whoever is attacking, and end the battle with a team-0 win only if team 0 is the side that benefits. (d) hoth.js:54: the ion cannon fires only when Hoth's defender is the light side. (e) warfront: pass tickets:false from layBattle (folded into proposal 2 if that lands first). (f) WarHud.jsx:12: render battleLine during the lull ('regrouping, the next in m:ss').
proposals.tests: battleScene.test.js: in an objectivesOn 'interdictor' battle the markers' keys are the Interdictor's gen-port and gen-star, and shield.show is called with the Interdictor. warpieces.test.js: with the Empire attacking and you on team 1, no hangar run is laid; with you on team 0 defending, shooting the reactor through ctx.mineAs blows it. Endor with the Empire attacking: Imperial shots on the moon generator don't count. Hoth with the Rebels attacking: no ion shots. warText and WarHud: the lull renders the regrouping line.

proposals.title: Objective plans: varied, seeded, multi-stage objective chains per kind and war
proposals.description:
New pure universe/battleObjectives.js, a type registry where each type has { make(spec, b), hit(o, from, to, dmg), targets(o, you), markers(o, you, team), progress(o, state) } and its tally keys. Types:
- destroy: a subsystem.
- group: k of n targets (turbolaser batteries on hulls, which already exist as TURRETS; shield-projector satellites placed round the objective ship; orbital defence platforms).
- zone: hold a radius-12 sphere. Pilots add seconds held to z:<id>:a or z:<id>:d plus a seeded AI curve; captured when a - d ≥ need. Used for a comms relay, slicing a data beacon (r 3, 15 s) and boarding.
- escort/intercept runners (proposal 3).
- wave: a bomber wave of N at scheduled time T aimed at the flagship or a station. Defender pilots' kills add to w:<k>; on arrival it deals (N - aiKills - kills)·9 chain HP to the defender.
- disable+board (the Tantive IV): destroy the corvette's engines subsystem, then zone-hold beside it for 20 s while a shuttle docks.
- ace hunt: the ace's HP from key ace:<team>, ×4 template HP, launching at a scheduled time.
- run: the existing run.js keys.
New universe/battlePlan.js: planFor({ kind, war, sys, id, sides, attacker, laid }) → { stages: [{ id, title: { attack, defend }, objectives, opensAt }], escalations, side }, picked with seeded('plan-' + battle.id) from menus in galaxy/battlePlans.js. Menus:
- assault: [gens ×2 | satellites 3 of 4 | flagship batteries 4 of 6] → [bridge | dorsal ion cannon] → [reactor], plus side objectives: ace hunt, defender bomber-wave intercepts at 180 and 390 s.
- siege: stage 0 [orbital platforms 3 of 5 (Coruscant, with world.war.planetShield) | Scarif's gate | Endor's moon generator], then the assault chain.
- interdiction: [gravity-well projectors 4 of 4 (the 2 domes plus 2 ventral; while they stand, the scene's interdicted input stays on) → bridge → reactor].
- blockade: [the picket: disable and board the lead corvette | its batteries 3 of 4] → runners launch on stage-1 fall or at 240 s.
- evacuation: attacker [the planetary ion cannon or the transports' Nebulon-B shield frigate] → [stop the transports]; defender mirrors.
- ambush: [survive 120 s: the convoy of 3 runners must have ≥1 alive] → [the jammer relay (zone)] → [break out].
War flavour: Clone Wars Lucrehulk 'droid control relay' (its fall freezes droid fighters for 30 s: vulture and trifighter mode 'dead'); Remnant 'Gideon's TIE Defender' ace; GCW Tantive IV boarding at Tatooine and Scarif. Per-system overrides in systems.js war.plan pin the set pieces (Endor: moon generator → Executor bridge → DS2 run). Say the dormant 'interdictor', 'blockade', 'escort' and 'gate' lines on the matching stage starts, plus a new crew key per stage type.
proposals.tests: planFor is a pure function: same input, deep-equal plan. Across 50 seeds every kind yields ≥2 distinct stage-1 objective types, and every type in the registry appears in some plan. Every plan has ascending opensAt, positive HP, and tally keys matching /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9:._-]{0,47}$/ with ≤80 keys a battle. Every placed objective (satellites, platforms, beacons) is reachable from outside, using the same bolts-from-all-round check as battle.test.js:27-66 (fraction > 0.25). Zone progress is net of the two sides and capped. A wave's arrival damage is reduced by each intercept. The Endor override yields the moon generator, then the Executor bridge, then the ds2-core run. Interdiction keeps the interdicted flag while the wells stand.

proposals.title: Fighter AI: commitment, balanced interception, strafing instead of orbiting
proposals.description: In battleAi.js, score targets with src/lib/ai/utility.js pick, with momentum 0.4, and keep the current target unless the best alternative scores ≤0.6× it, with a minimum commit of 2.5 s for dogfighters. Bombers choose a target at the start of a run and keep it until the torpedo fires or the target dies (replacing the per-retarget re-roll at battle.js:454-461 and 399-415). Defender bombers target a seeded capital per flight, not a random hull point each tick. Raise the interceptor's bomber weight from 0.12 to 0.35 and cap interceptors a bomber at min(3, ceil(enemyBombers/2)) with squad.js createTokens({ pools: { intercept: 3 } }). When no enemy fighter is within 80, a dogfighter flies strafing runs like a bomber: at the nearest enemy battery (a hit costs it 1 HP, so AI can silence batteries) or at the phase objective (counting as aiShare for cosmetic impacts under the director). It never heads to C idle.
proposals.tests: At a fixed 1/30 step in each of the 7 kinds: dogfighter target switches ≤0.25/s each; bombers switch ≤2 times a life; both sides' bombers fire ≥15 torpedoes in the first 180 s; Imperial TIE bomber median life ≥10 s at Yavin. After the enemy fighters are all down (perSide 4, tickets 0 for the defender), no attacker fighter goes >3 s without a target while enemy capitals are alive, and batteries take hits.

proposals.title: Squads, roles, reinforcement waves and retreat
proposals.description:
In battleAi.js, give each side flights of 3 assigned by spawn index (flight = floor(i/3)); the first alive member leads:
- The leader picks the flight's target (focus fire). Wingmen take the leader's target, or the leader's chaser when leader.chased is within 0.6 s.
- In transit (>40 from the target), wingmen hold formation offsets (±3 to the side, 2 back).
- Each bomber flight gets one escort flight, which engages whatever targets those bombers.
- Defender interceptors fly CAP: they stay within 50 of the objective ship and engage anything entering it.
Objective awareness: each objective keeps a threat score (damage in the last 10 s, plus enemies within 40). Defender fighter scoring adds 2× weight for enemies within 40 of the most threatened objective.
Retreat: hp ≤35% sets mode 'rtb' toward its side's carrier hangar point (a cap with a hangar: destroyer, venator, moncal, lucrehulk, executor, acclamator). After 6 s within 10 of it, the fighter is back at full HP; no ticket is spent.
Waves replace the 3-6 s individual respawn: the attacker's every 20 s and the defender's every 30 s, launched together from the hangar points on the battle clock (deterministic). The plan's escalations add a bomber wave of 6 at 180 and 390 s, the ace at 240 s, and a reserve squadron at the final push (480 s).
Retreat also uses squad.js confidence and posture: a flight whose nerve is 'panicked' (3 to 1 against) breaks for home.
proposals.tests: Flights: in 60 s, ≥70% of a flight's alive members share a target at any sample. A fighter at 30% HP reaches its hangar point and comes back at full HP without a ticket spent. Waves: arrivals happen only at multiples of the wave period (± one step), and with a fixed seed and step the wave times are identical across runs. CAP: defender interceptors' mean distance to the objective ship is <60 while bombers attack it. Performance: 64 fighters, 1200 updates, under the existing 4 s budget.

proposals.title: Capital ship AI: fleet focus fire, final push and broadsides, jump-outs
proposals.description: In battleCapitals.js, every 15 s each side picks a fleet focus target: the attacker focuses the objective ship; the defender focuses the most damaged attacker capital or the attacker's flagship. 60% of batteries fire at the focus, the rest at the nearest enemy capital. Keep the 40% near-miss rate only for non-focus shots. At the plan's final push (480 s), the attacker's escorts advance 1.2 units a second toward the centre for 40 s (moveCapital), and both lines' escorts turn up to 25° to bring a flank to bear (turnCapital). Each move calls ctx.moveHull so the ship's collision solids follow. An escort under 15% hull jumps out (a new 'jumped' event: a flash, then gone, not counted as destroyed). After 'over', the losing fleet's surviving capitals jump out one every 3 s, and its fighters RTB.
proposals.tests: Over 60 s, ≥55% of a side's turbo shots aim at the focus target. At 480-520 s the attacker's escorts are ≥30 units nearer the centre, with their spheres, turrets and subs moved by the same displacement (the existing 'moves and turns a capital' test pattern). An escort at 10% hull emits 'jumped' and is removed without a 'capital' event. After over, the losing side's capitals are gone within count×3+1 s.

proposals.title: Pacing, escalation, end card and lull
proposals.description:
Default 10-minute arc, given as plan.escalations (pure data):
- 0-90 s: opening. Fighter screens clash, the first stage is open but the attacker's capitals are out of range.
- 150 s and 300 s: stage gates.
- 180 and 390 s: bomber waves.
- 240 s: the ace launches.
- 480 s: final push (AI pressure ×1.5, capitals advance, defender reserve).
- 600 s: clock end.
warfront.info gains stage, objectives (shared HP from the director), escalation next-at and result { winner, why, yours: { kills, objectives, intercepts, points } }. New BattleEnd.jsx shows Victory/Defeat for 8 s, with why in words ('The reactor went', 'Six transports got away', 'Held out to the end'), your contribution and the points added. WarHud gains a compact stage line and up to 3 objective bars, 'Victory at Hoth · next battle in m:ss' after an early end, and the lull line. After over, fighters RTB and the losing fleet jumps out rather than milling for minutes. warText gets pure formatters for these.
proposals.tests: warText.test.js: formatters for stage, objective bars, result and lull lines. warfront.test.js: info.result is set once on over and matches the director's winner; after over no fighter fires, and the losing capitals jump out. Plan test: escalation times are ascending and inside [0, length].

proposals.title: Local dynamic difficulty, never touching the shared outcome
proposals.tests: difficulty is monotone in kills and deaths and bounded to [0.6, 1.6]. At d=1, a pilot circling the attacked objective (ai.mjs's script at r 14, 0.7 rad/s) takes 3-7 shield/s, against 5.0 today. At d=0.6 that drops by ≥30%. The director state is identical at d=0.6 and d=1.6 for the same tally.

constraints: Rules stay pure and deterministic: no three.js and no Math.random in battle, director, plan, objective or AI modules. Randomness comes from the passed rand or gcw.js seeded(text): battle rand is seeded(b.id) (warfront.js:207) and layout is seeded(`lay-${seed}`) (battles.js:288). scarif.js uses Math.random only for flashes, which is acceptable.

File size: scripts/health/big-files.mjs CEILING 1500 and WARN 800 lines per src file. battle.js is 1018 today, already over WARN, so new code goes in new modules (battleAi, battleCapitals, battleRunners, battleObjectives, battlePlan, battleDirector, battleDifficulty), each under 800.

Tally limits (universe/tally.js): keys match /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9:._-]{0,47}$/; values only grow (shares), value = max(sum of shares, floor); 96 keys a message by default; the fight tally is capped at 4000 per pilot per key (warfront.js:78). The fight epoch is the battle id. The `fight` action is rate-limited [2,6] (protocol.js:87).
Teams: team 0 is the light side and team 1 the dark side whoever attacks; the Hutts take the missing slot (gcw.js teamsOf). The set pieces hard-code REBELS=0 and EMPIRE=1.

Public battle interface used elsewhere must keep working: front.js (universe map wars, default options, Math.random), warfront.js, battleScene.js and the set pieces use teams, capitals, fighters, runners, bolts, phase, clock, over, you, attacker, defender, lines, radius, length, setYou, update(dt, you) → events, hit, fire, targets, info, end, disable, wreck, moveCapital, turnCapital and addRunner. New behaviour must be opt-in through createBattle options so the universe wars are unchanged.

Pinned tests: battle.test.js (objectives reachable from outside >25%, shield holds till gens are down, phases in order, ticket end 'as it always has, unless told not to', runners win and lose, ion disable, batteries, move/turn capital, 64 fighters for 1200 updates in under 4 s, ends within its clock at dt 1/20); battles.test.js (six kinds with text, objective and runners; templates; layBattle shape; interdiction objectives; runners side; ambush 1 escort and more fighters; clear of the planet); warpieces.test.js (Endor, Hoth, Scarif and hangar flows); warfront.test.js (shared damage, objective down by other pilots, win counted once).

GCW timing: step 12 min, fight 10 min, lull 2 min (gcw.js:54-55); battle ids and seeds are `${epoch}.${war}.${sys}.${step}` (gcw.js:341-344). Points: objective 3, kill 0.1, turret 0.5, win 10, intercept 1, ace 2 (gcw.js:61).
The unsworn pilot is nobody's target and scores nothing (warfront.js:217-230); reduced motion disables battles entirely (scene.js:273).

The galaxy's ships are scaled at 53.3 m a map unit (battles.js SIZE), and fighters' speeds are paced ×0.6 (wars.js F → ship.js paced, PACE = 12/20). Lines are ≥70 apart from the centre and the radius is lines+60.
No browser check was required for this area; checks scripts/galaxy-war-check.mjs and galaxy-setpieces-check.mjs drive war.force and war.skip (dt 0.1), so they must keep working with a fixed-step sim.
openQuestions: Will the owner accept the AI's effect on objectives, runners and capital deaths becoming a shared scripted pressure curve, with the local dogfight as spectacle and player interaction? The fleet-war spec (rev 2, lines 228-229) intended exactly that, and it is the only way for every pilot to see the same battle and winner. The alternative is a hybrid, where local AI damage is capped to the curve.

What target win rates and lengths are wanted? Suggested: AI-only attacker wins 30-60% of battles, decided at 7:30-10:00; a solo pilot wins at about 4:30-7:30; 4+ pilots never before about 5:00 (stage gates).

Should defender pilots get a shared lever (intercept credits reducing AI pressure, zone holds, runner cover)? It needs a team-aware ctx.mineAs and new tally keys, but no protocol change: fight messages carry any valid keys.

Should tickets survive at all in the galaxy? Today they end liberator attacks in about 2-3.5 min at 60 Hz. The proposal passes tickets:false and uses waves plus RTB instead; tickets could remain as HUD flavour derived from the director.
How many pilots joined each side: count with a `here:a`/`here:d` key that each pilot adds 1 to once (no tally API change), or add a peers-with-share count to tally.js?

Should a battle decided early (e.g. at 6:00) start the next one sooner? gcw.js steps are fixed 12-minute wall-clock windows; the proposal keeps them and fills the rest with the end card, the losing fleet's jump-out and a 'next battle in' line.

Which set-piece plans per system (systems.js war.plan overrides) should be pinned vs seeded? E.g. Endor always moon generator → Executor bridge → DS2 run; Scarif always gate; Hoth always ion cannon plus transports.
Is the universe map's Rick and Morty / Breaking Bad front (front.js, local and unshared) meant to get the same director and plans, or stay as is?
